books/clean-architecture/intro.title: Clean Architecture — Book Overview
books/clean-architecture/intro.description: A comprehensive overview of "Clean Architecture: A Craftsman's Guide to Software Structure and Design" by Robert C. Martin. Understand the goals, structure, and key takeaways before diving into each chapter.

books/clean-architecture/part1-introduct.title: Chapter 1: What Is Design and Architecture?
books/clean-architecture/part1-introduct.description: Martin demolishes the false distinction between "design" and "architecture", then presents the singular goal of software architecture: minimizing the human effort required to build and maintain a system.

books/clean-architecture/part1-introduct.title: Chapter 2: A Tale of Two Values
books/clean-architecture/part1-introduct.description: Every software system delivers two values — behavior and structure. Martin argues that structure (architecture) is almost always the more important of the two, yet teams chronically neglect it. Learn to use Eisenhower's Matrix to fight for architectural health.

books/clean-architecture/part2-programmi.title: Chapter 3: Paradigm Overview
books/clean-architecture/part2-programmi.description: The three programming paradigms — structured, object-oriented, and functional — each impose discipline by removing capabilities from the programmer. Martin shows how each paradigm maps directly to a fundamental concern of software architecture.

books/clean-architecture/part2-programmi.title: Chapter 4: Structured Programming
books/clean-architecture/part2-programmi.description: Dijkstra's discovery that unrestrained goto is harmful, and how structured programming's sequence/selection/iteration constructs make software provable — and testable. The scientific method applied to code.

books/clean-architecture/part2-programmi.title: Chapter 5: Object-Oriented Programming
books/clean-architecture/part2-programmi.description: Martin revisits the three pillars of OOP — encapsulation, inheritance, and polymorphism — and argues that OO's true architectural gift is safe, convenient polymorphism that enables plugin architecture and dependency inversion.

books/clean-architecture/part2-programmi.title: Chapter 6: Functional Programming
books/clean-architecture/part2-programmi.description: Functional programming's core discipline — immutability — eliminates entire classes of concurrency bugs. Learn how immutability, segregation of mutability, and event sourcing shape modern system design.

books/clean-architecture/part3-design-pr.title: Chapter 7: SRP — The Single Responsibility Principle
books/clean-architecture/part3-design-pr.description: The most misunderstood SOLID principle. SRP is NOT "every class does one thing" — it means a module should have only one reason to change, i.e., it serves only one actor. Learn the two symptoms of SRP violation and how to solve them.

books/clean-architecture/part3-design-pr.title: Chapter 8: OCP — The Open-Closed Principle
books/clean-architecture/part3-design-pr.description: A software artifact should be open for extension but closed for modification. OCP is the architectural goal that drives Clean Architecture: protect high-level policy from changes in low-level details by controlling the direction of dependencies.

books/clean-architecture/part3-design-pr.title: Chapter 9: LSP — The Liskov Substitution Principle
books/clean-architecture/part3-design-pr.description: If S is a subtype of T, objects of type S must be substitutable for objects of type T without altering the correctness of the program. LSP governs not just inheritance but any interface contract — and its violation breaks architectural boundaries.

books/clean-architecture/part3-design-pr.title: Chapter 10: ISP — The Interface Segregation Principle
books/clean-architecture/part3-design-pr.description: No client should be forced to depend on methods it does not use. ISP keeps interfaces focused, prevents unnecessary recompilation, and — at the architectural level — prevents importing modules that drag in unwanted dependencies.

books/clean-architecture/part3-design-pr.title: Chapter 11: DIP — The Dependency Inversion Principle
books/clean-architecture/part3-design-pr.description: High-level policy should not depend on low-level details. Both should depend on abstractions. DIP is the mechanism that makes Clean Architecture possible — and the most architecturally consequential of all SOLID principles.

books/clean-architecture/part4-component.title: Chapter 12: Components
books/clean-architecture/part4-component.description: Components are the units of deployment — JARs, DLLs, shared libraries. Martin traces their history from early relocatable binaries to modern package managers, establishing the foundation for the component cohesion and coupling principles that follow.

books/clean-architecture/part4-component.title: Chapter 13: Component Cohesion
books/clean-architecture/part4-component.description: Three principles govern which classes belong in which component: REP (Reuse/Release Equivalence), CCP (Common Closure), and CRP (Common Reuse). They form a tension triangle — understanding the trade-offs helps you choose the right grouping strategy for your project's stage.

books/clean-architecture/part4-component.title: Chapter 14: Component Coupling
books/clean-architecture/part4-component.description: Three principles govern dependencies between components: ADP (no dependency cycles), SDP (depend in the direction of stability), and SAP (stable components should be abstract). These principles shape large-scale architecture and determine which components can evolve independently.

books/clean-architecture/part5-architect.title: Chapter 15: What Is Architecture?
books/clean-architecture/part5-architect.description: Architecture is the shape of a system — the decisions that divide a system into components, arrange those components, and specify how they communicate. A good architect maximizes the number of decisions NOT made, keeping options open as long as possible.

books/clean-architecture/part5-architect.title: Chapter 16: Independence
books/clean-architecture/part5-architect.description: A good architecture supports independent developability, deployability, and operability. Martin explains the use-case, operational, and deployment decoupling modes and why the monolith-vs-microservices decision can and should be deferred.

books/clean-architecture/part5-architect.title: Chapters 17–20: Boundaries, Business Rules & Policy
books/clean-architecture/part5-architect.description: Boundaries separate software elements and restrict knowledge between them. This section covers drawing lines between components, anatomy of boundaries, policy levels, entities, and use cases — the core of Clean Architecture.

books/clean-architecture/part5-architect.title: Chapters 21–25: Screaming, Clean & Testable Architecture
books/clean-architecture/part5-architect.description: The architecture should scream the system's intent. Clean Architecture's four concentric rings define the dependency rule in practice. Testable architectures, Humble Objects, and partial boundaries complete the practical application model.

books/clean-architecture/part5-architect.title: Chapters 27–29: Main Component, Services & Test Boundary
books/clean-architecture/part5-architect.description: The Main Component is the dirtiest place in the system — where everything is wired together. Services are not architecturally special. Tests are a component too — they must respect boundaries or become a maintenance burden.

books/clean-architecture/part6-details/c.title: Chapters 30–32: The Database, Web & Frameworks Are Details
books/clean-architecture/part6-details/c.description: Databases, web frameworks, and all third-party frameworks are details — implementation choices that should be deferred and hidden behind boundaries. Learn why treating them as the center of your architecture leads to rigidity and how to protect your business rules from them.

technical-knowledge/dsa/leetcode-daily.description: Get your daily LeetCode challenge, pick a random problem from our curated set, or explore by topic.

technical-knowledge/dsa/week-1-arrays-st.title: Week 1: Arrays, Strings & Prefix Sums
technical-knowledge/dsa/week-1-arrays-st.description: Master contiguous memory structures in Java, including static arrays and string immutability, and optimize range queries using the Prefix Sum pattern.

technical-knowledge/dsa/week-10-recursio.title: Week 10: Recursion & Backtracking
technical-knowledge/dsa/week-10-recursio.description: Master the art of recursive thinking and the 'Choose-Explore-Unchoose' pattern. Learn to solve complex combinatorial problems like permutations, combinations, and grid-based searches in Java.

technical-knowledge/dsa/week-11-interval.title: Week 11: Intervals & Sweep Line Algorithms
technical-knowledge/dsa/week-11-interval.description: Master scheduling problems, overlapping events, and the Sweep Line algorithm. Learn how to efficiently sort and process 2D arrays and objects in Java.

technical-knowledge/dsa/week-12-heaps-gr.title: Week 12: Heaps (Priority Queues) & Greedy Algorithms
technical-knowledge/dsa/week-12-heaps-gr.description: Conclude Phase 3 by mastering dynamic extremum tracking and locally optimal choices. Dive deep into Java's PriorityQueue, Top K patterns, and Greedy state transitions.

technical-knowledge/dsa/week-13-dynamic-.title: Week 13: Dynamic Programming I (1D)
technical-knowledge/dsa/week-13-dynamic-.description: Enter Phase 4 by conquering Dynamic Programming. Learn to identify overlapping subproblems and map recursion to bottom-up tabulation and memoization in Java.

technical-knowledge/dsa/week-14-dynamic-.title: Week 14: Dynamic Programming II (2D)
technical-knowledge/dsa/week-14-dynamic-.description: Master multi-dimensional Dynamic Programming. Learn to solve Grid Traversals, String Alignments (LCS, Edit Distance), and 2D space optimization in Java.

technical-knowledge/dsa/week-15-advanced.title: Week 15: Advanced Sliding Windows
technical-knowledge/dsa/week-15-advanced.description: Master the variable-size sliding window pattern in Java. Learn to dynamically expand and shrink boundaries to solve complex substring, subarray, and stream processing problems.

technical-knowledge/dsa/week-16-tries-pr.title: Week 16: Tries (Prefix Trees)
technical-knowledge/dsa/week-16-tries-pr.description: Master the Trie data structure for lightning-fast string manipulation. Learn to build Autocomplete systems, handle wildcard searches, and optimize multi-word grid searches in Java.

technical-knowledge/dsa/week-17-shortest.title: Week 17: Shortest Paths & MST
technical-knowledge/dsa/week-17-shortest.description: Begin Phase 5 by conquering weighted graphs. Master Dijkstra's Algorithm for finding the shortest path and Prim's Algorithm for building Minimum Spanning Trees in Java.

technical-knowledge/dsa/week-18-disjoint.title: Week 18: Disjoint Set Union (Union-Find)
technical-knowledge/dsa/week-18-disjoint.description: Master the Disjoint Set Union (DSU) data structure. Learn how to dynamically track connected components and optimize with Path Compression and Union by Rank in Java.

technical-knowledge/dsa/week-19-bit-mani.title: Week 19: Bit Manipulation & Math
technical-knowledge/dsa/week-19-bit-mani.description: Shift from high-level data structures to low-level CPU operations. Master XOR properties, Bit Masking, signed vs. unsigned shifts, and core Number Theory in Java.

technical-knowledge/dsa/week-2-two-point.title: Week 2: Two Pointers & Basic Sliding Window
technical-knowledge/dsa/week-2-two-point.description: Master the Two Pointers and fixed-size Sliding Window techniques in Java to optimize nested loops and achieve O(N) time complexity for array and string traversals.

technical-knowledge/dsa/week-20-comprehe.title: Week 20: Comprehensive Review & System Design Mappings
technical-knowledge/dsa/week-20-comprehe.description: The final week! Synthesize all DSA patterns, map abstract data structures to real-world Java backend systems, and master technical interview communication.

technical-knowledge/dsa/week-3-linked-li.title: Week 3: Linked Lists & Fast/Slow Pointers
technical-knowledge/dsa/week-3-linked-li.description: Transition from contiguous arrays to node-based data structures. Master reference manipulation, Dummy Nodes, and the Fast & Slow Pointer technique in Java.

technical-knowledge/dsa/week-4-hash-tabl.title: Week 4: Hash Tables & Sets
technical-knowledge/dsa/week-4-hash-tabl.description: Master Hash Maps and Hash Sets in Java. Learn about O(1) lookups, collision resolution, frequency counting, and the equals() and hashCode() contract.

technical-knowledge/dsa/week-5-stacks-qu.title: Week 5: Stacks, Queues & Monotonic Stack
technical-knowledge/dsa/week-5-stacks-qu.description: Transition to Phase 2 by mastering LIFO and FIFO data structures. Learn why to avoid Java's legacy Stack class and dive deep into the highly-tested Monotonic Stack pattern.

technical-knowledge/dsa/week-6-binary-tr.title: Week 6: Binary Trees & BSTs
technical-knowledge/dsa/week-6-binary-tr.description: Move from linear to hierarchical data structures. Master Depth-First Search (DFS), Breadth-First Search (BFS), and the properties of Binary Search Trees in Java.

technical-knowledge/dsa/week-7-graph-fou.title: Week 7: Graph Foundations
technical-knowledge/dsa/week-7-graph-fou.description: Transition from trees to general networks. Master graph representations, Adjacency Lists, and grid-based DFS/BFS traversals in Java.

technical-knowledge/dsa/week-8-advanced-.title: Week 8: Advanced Graph Concepts
technical-knowledge/dsa/week-8-advanced-.description: Master Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs), cycle detection in directed graphs, and dependency resolution using Kahn's Algorithm (Topological Sort) in Java.

technical-knowledge/dsa/week-9-binary-se.title: Week 9: Binary Search & The Answer Space
technical-knowledge/dsa/week-9-binary-se.description: Start Phase 3 by mastering logarithmic time complexity. Learn standard Binary Search, handling rotated arrays, and the advanced "Binary Search on Answer Space" pattern in Java.

technical-knowledge/elasticsearch/elasti.description: A deep dive into Elasticsearch internals — covering the inverted index structure, node roles, sharding, document write path, and search query execution.
